sections.section_title:
Q.1 Choose the correct answer of the following (any seven question
                    only):

questions.text: Increasing the air gap in an induction motor generally leads to:
options: Increased magnetic flux and improved efficiency
Reduced magnetizing inductance and a lower power factor

questions.text:
In V/f control (voltage-to-frequency control), if both voltage and frequency are reduced while
                        keeping the ratio constant, the maximum torque of the motor:
Hysteresis motors are particularly suited for applications requiring:
options: High starting torque under heavy loads
Precise speed control with low ripple
High torque density for industrial drives

questions.text: One disadvantage often encountered with reluctance motors is:
options: High maintenance due to brush wear

questions.text: The term "step angle" in a stepper motor refers to:
options: The angle between the stator poles
The maximum rotation of the motor at full load
The angular displacement per input pulse
The phase shift between different windings

questions.text: In a brushless DC motor, electronic commutation is performed by:
options: The natural inductance of the stator

questions.text: Short-pitch (or chorded) windings are used in AC machines primarily to:
options: Reduce the harmonic content (with a slight reduction in fundamental EMF)
Increase the number of coils per phase

questions.text: Compared to a distributed winding, a concentrated winding:
options: Produces an EMF with a more sinusoidal waveform
Exhibits a lower distribution factor, leading to higher harmonic content
Is always used for high-power applications

questions.text:
At the minimum point on the V-curve of a synchronous machine, the armature current is minimum
                        because:
options:
The armature reaction is minimized (approximately balanced), leading to nearly unity power
                            factor

questions.text: When two alternators are paralleled. if one is over-excited and the other under-excited. then:
options: Both will share active load equally regardless of excitation

The over-excited unit will supply reactive power while the under-excited unit will absorb
                            reactive power
The alternators will not be able to share load at all
Only the over-excited alternator will supply both active and reactive power
